title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the student-led hubs, late-night study nooks, and quiet natural retreats that define daily life at Connecticut College beyond the official tour path.

cards.title: The MOBROC Barn
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Music Practice Space
cards.notes: Practice or watch student bands in this converted squash court. It features a full sound system and a second-level balcony for viewing live rehearsals.
cards.short_summary: A student-run music practice and performance venue managed by Musicians Organized for Bands Rights on Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Barn (or MOBROC Barn) is a student-run practice and performance space in a converted squash court with a sound system and balcony.
cards.access_notes: Primarily used by MOBROC member bands for practice and scheduled student performances.

cards.title: Coffee Grounds
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Café in Katharine Blunt House
cards.notes: Visit this cozy, student-managed coffee shop for a quiet study session. It is known for its relaxed atmosphere and is located inside the KB residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A popular student-run café located on the first floor of Katharine Blunt House, offering a social study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffee Grounds is a student-run coffee shop located in Katharine Blunt House.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; hours are typically posted at the entrance and managed by student staff.

cards.title: Blue Camel Café
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Study Space in Shain Library
cards.notes: Utilize this first-floor café area for late-night cramming. While the counter closes, the seating area remains accessible 24/7 for students with ID.
cards.short_summary: A central campus café that doubles as a 24-hour study lounge for students within the Charles E. Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Camel Café is located on the first floor of Shain Library and doubles as a 24-hour study space.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: The seating area is accessible 24 hours a day for students with a valid Camel Card.

cards.title: Unity House Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Communal Cooking and Gathering Space
cards.notes: Prepare a meal with friends in this fully equipped kitchen. It serves as a central social hub for students of all backgrounds to share food and culture.
cards.short_summary: A communal kitchen and lounge area within the Unity House multicultural center used for student gatherings and meal preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: Unity House features a kitchen available for campus community members to prepare meals and host events.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours (typically 8:30 am to 10:00 pm) for student use.

cards.title: Ruane's Den
cards.subtitle: Walk-In Coffee Closet in Harkness House
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner in this south campus coffee shop. It features big-screen TVs and comfortable seating, making it ideal for group meetings or solo study.
cards.short_summary: A student-run coffee shop and social space located on the first floor of Harkness Residence Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruane's Den is a student-run café location in Harkness Residence Hall with comfy seating and big-screen TVs.
cards.access_notes: Located within a residence hall; accessible to the college community during operating hours.

cards.title: The Granite Classroom
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Learning Space on Tempel Green
cards.notes: Attend a class or study outdoors at this granite-fashioned classroom. It offers expansive views of the Long Island Sound and the Thames River.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor classroom made of granite located on Tempel Green, used for both formal instruction and informal student study.
cards.evidence_claim: Tempel Green features an outdoor classroom fashioned from granite where some professors move their classes.
cards.access_notes: Open public space on the main campus green; available for use when not occupied by a scheduled class.

cards.title: Caroline Black Garden
cards.subtitle: Quiet Arboretum Retreat
cards.notes: Escape the campus bustle in this 4-acre garden. It is a favorite spot for students seeking a peaceful environment for reflection or quiet reading.
cards.short_summary: A diverse botanical collection within the Arboretum, serving as a tranquil space for recreation and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Caroline Black Garden is a 4-acre part of the Arboretum used for recreation and reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public from sunrise to sunset, 365 days a year.

cards.title: Hillel House Great Room
cards.subtitle: Study and Social Space
cards.notes: Study in the Great Room or relax on the couches downstairs. This space offers a quiet library and a welcoming atmosphere for students of all faiths.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose space within the Zachs Hillel House used for studying, lectures, and community dinners.
cards.evidence_claim: Zachs Hillel House features a great room for studying, lectures, and dinners, plus a library and downstairs lounge with comfy chairs.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; building hours typically follow standard campus facility schedules.

cards.title: The White Box Gallery
cards.subtitle: Student Exhibition Space
cards.notes: View rotating student work in this dedicated exhibition space. It provides a professional-style gallery setting for course projects and senior thesis work.
cards.short_summary: A modern exhibition space within the Cummings Arts Center specifically for student art displays and special projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cummings Arts Center houses a white-box gallery for student exhibitions and special course projects.
cards.access_notes: Open during Cummings Arts Center building hours; exhibitions change periodically throughout the semester.

cards.title: Harkness Chapel Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet Lower-Level Study Nook
cards.notes: Discover this secluded library on the lower level of the chapel. It is one of the quietest spots on campus for focused reading and research.
cards.short_summary: A small, quiet library and meeting area located in the lower level of the historic Harkness Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: In the lower level of Harkness Chapel are offices, meeting rooms, and a library.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during chapel building hours; check the online calendar for event-related closures.
